ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, line $AB$ and line $CD$ intersect at point $O$, $\angle DOE = 90^\circ$, $OD$ bisects $\angle BOF$, $\angle BOE = 50^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle AOF$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the given conditions, we have
\[
\angle AOF = 180^\circ - \angle AOC - \angle DOF = 180^\circ - 40^\circ - 40^\circ = \boxed{100^\circ}.
\]

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} From the given conditions, we have \[ \angle AOF = 180^\circ - \angle AOC - \angle DOF = 180^\circ - 40^\circ - 40^\circ = \boxed{100^\circ}. \]
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, AB is a slanted straight line passing through O, OA points to the lower left, and OB points to the upper right, so OA and OB are opposite rays; CD is a horizontal straight line passing through O, OC points left, and OD points right; OE goes vertically upward from O, and in the figure a right-angle mark is drawn between OE and OD; OB is located inside the right angle ∠EOD in the upper right; OF points from O to the lower right. Reasoning: It is known that ∠DOE = 90°, and ∠BOE = 50°. Since OB is inside ∠EOD, ∠BOD = 90° - 50° = 40°. Also because OD bisects ∠BOF, ∠DOF = ∠BOD = 40°, thus ∠BOF = 40° + 40° = 80°. Since OA and OB are opposite rays, ∠AOF and ∠BOF form a pair of adjacent supplementary angles, therefore ∠AOF = 180° - 80° = 100°. Final answer: 100°.
